statement: For offline BPP, a score_item priority that mixes item size (descending, BFD-like) with a residual-capacity-structure term will reduce bin count versus pure size-descending first-fit when repacking: ordering large-but-awkward items first minimizes fragmentation in the residual capacity signature of open bins.
rationale: No KB entries are available for this release (kb_search returned 0 hits for both template-specific and classic BFD queries), and list_interfaces reports an empty template registry, so the plan must rely on the single allowed template bpp_offline_reorder_repack with postprocess none. Classical offline BPP results (FFD/BFD ordering) show ordering dominates quality; a residual-capacity-aware priority is a low-risk superset of size-descending order that should never be worse after repack.

statement: For offline BPP, a score_item priority that mixes item size (descending, BFD-like) with a residual-capacity-structure term will reduce bin count versus pure size-descending first-fit when repacking: ordering large-but-awkward items first minimizes fragmentation in the residual capacity signature of open bins.
rationale: Round 1 realized the plain size-descending variant (evolved hook `sorted((-size, i))`), i.e. the BFD-like control arm, not the residual-capacity-aware arm. It achieved 36/36 feasible at mean 28.083 bins with 0.215 ms mean solve time against a 500 ms budget — so ordering quality, not runtime, is the binding constraint and there is ~2000x runtime headroom to spend on a richer priority score. Hypothesis remains open pending an explicit residual-capacity/fragmentation term in score_item.

rationale: Round 1 only realized the size-descending control arm (mean 28.083 bins, 36/36 feasible, 0.215 ms/solve), so the residual-capacity term is still unmeasured; runtime headroom is ~2000x, making a richer score_item the highest-leverage round-2 move.

statement: For offline BPP, a score_item priority that mixes item size (descending, BFD-like) with a residual-capacity-structure term will reduce bin count versus pure size-descending first-fit when repacking: ordering large-but-awkward items first minimizes fragmentation in the residual capacity signature of open bins.
rationale: Round 2 submitted the composite score_item (size + residual-capacity tightness + awkwardness proxy, best-fit repack placement) under bpp_offline_reorder_repack with postprocess none. The round-2 evaluation artifact (agent_artifacts/round_0002_dev_eval.json, sha256 7430c0e6...) returned null for instance_count, completion_rate, all_feasible, mean_tour_length and solve_ms_mean, so no objective signal was recorded for the residual-capacity term. The hypothesis therefore remains UNMEASURED, not refuted: no evidence yet that the tightness term helps or hurts bin count versus the 28.0833-bin size-descending control from round 1. Kept in 'testing' with an unchanged statement; round 3 must either reproduce a scored evaluation of the same composite score_item or fall back to a controlled A/B (pure size-descending vs. size+tightness) on the size-50/size-100 regimes where the VBS gap is largest (2.30%/2.20%), which are the regimes where ordering-induced fragmentation should first show up.
